newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Arco sees Australian coal mine sales soon.
newsitem.headline: Arco sees Australian coal mine sales soon.

text.p: Arco Coal Australia Inc, part of U.S. energy giant Atlantic Richfield Co, said on Monday it was seeking buyers for its Blair Athol, Gordonstone and Clermont coal mines in central Queensland with expressions of interest expected from global and local groups.

"It (the sale) should be sooner rather than later," Arco Coal president Bill Wagener told Reuters. Information memorandum documents were expected to be sent out to interested parties in about a week's time, he said.
Wegener said the sale of the group's remaining Curragh open cut mine was being delayed due to the uncertainty surrounding a miners' dispute, now in its 15th week.
Arco's decision to sell the three mines followed an earlier announcement in April that Arco's coal mines could be the subject of either a trade sale or a float.
Wagener said the option for a float had faded in recent weeks with an outright sale thought to be the better outcome.
The mines produce about 23 million tonnes of coal a year and represent about 20 percent of Queensland's total production.
"We are not interested in a fire sale of the assets, certainly not Curragh," Wagener said.

Analysts said that with Blair Athol and Clermont likely to be taken by joint venture partner Rio Tinto Ltd under pre-emptive agreements, the Gordonstone (coking coal) and Curragh (thermal coal) mines could be worth up to A$600 million as a straight trade sale.

The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd has already expressed an interest in both Gordonstone and Curragh while Shell Australia Ltd, MIM Holdings Ltd and QCT Resources Ltd are all possible buyers, coal analysts said.

Blair Athol, purchased in a joint venture with Pacific Coal and two Japanese partners in 1977, was a 10 million tonnes-a-year thermal coal mine while Clermont was a greenfields operation also bought as a joint venture with Pacific Coal about two years ago, Wagener said.
The 80 percent Arco-owned Gordonstone mine was bought in 1989 and was capable of producing 6.5 million tonnes annually run-of-mine hard coking coal.
Curragh is capable of producing 3.5 million tonnes of mainly thermal coal annually.
Wagener said Arco had called for a restart of production at Curragh, despite ongoing industrial action over demarcation issues and the use of contractors.
"The thing we have tried to do is adopt patience in the negotiation process," Wagener said.
"We've given it a good go," he said.
Arco had called for train deliveries to start on a daily basis this week. "All we can do is call for the trains. It (now) is an issue for Queensland Rail," Wagener said.
Arco had an 87 percent stake in Curragh with Japanese coal giant Mitsui & Co holding the balance.

Wagener said in April the sale of Atlantic Richfield's global coal assets would mean the end of Arco Coal's presence in Australia. The decision to withdraw from Australia however was strategic and had nothing to do with under-performance, he said.
The decision was aimed at boosting shareholder returns and sharpening the company's focus on oil and gas and specialty chemicals, he said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
